result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.average_neighbor_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute average neighbor degree for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19536-L19700){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.average_neighbor_degree( source="out", target="out", weight=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Average neighbor degree](/assets/graphs/average-neighbor-degree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by the mean degree of each node's neighbors. A has only two neighbors, but they are B (degree 3) and the hub C (degree 4), so A tops the table at 3.50, ahead of D 3.33, while the hub C itself scores 2.75." width="100%"} For each node, calculates the average degree of its neighbors. This metric helps analyze degree correlations and mixing patterns in networks, indicating whether nodes tend to connect to similar-degree neighbors (assortative) or different-degree neighbors (disassortative). For undirected graphs, computes the average degree of all neighbors. For directed graphs, the `source` parameter controls which neighbors to consider, and the `target` parameter controls how to measure their degrees. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : For directed graphs only, specifies which neighbors to consider: (1) `"out"` for out-neighbors (successors), (2) `"in"` for in-neighbors (predecessors), and (3) `"in+out"` for both in-neighbors and out-neighbors. Raises error if used with undirected graphs. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : For directed graphs only, specifies how to measure neighbor degrees: (1) `"out"` for out-neighbors (successors), (2) `"in"` for in-neighbors (predecessors), and (3) `"in+out"` for both in-neighbors and out-neighbors. Raises error if used with undirected graphs. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute name containing weights. If provided, computes weighted average using: `k_nn,i = (1 / s_i) * Σ_j w_ij * k_j`, where `s_i` is the weighted degree. Currently not implemented and will raise error if specified. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of node attribute to store results. If `None`, uses `average_neighbor_degree`. Only used when `return_dict=False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dict mapping node labels to average neighbor degrees. If `False`, stores values in graph and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node ID to average neighbor degree. If `return_dict=False`: self (for method chaining). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : - if graph is empty - if `source` or `target` parameters are used with undirected graphs - if `source` or `target` values are invalid - if `weight` is specified (not yet implemented) ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For each node $v$, this returns the mean degree of the nodes adjacent to $v$: $k_{nn}(v) = \dfrac{1}{|N(v)|} \sum_{u \in N(v)} k(u)$. Aggregating that quantity across degree classes reveals a network's mixing pattern: an assortative graph has high-degree nodes preferentially connected to other high-degree nodes, so $k_{nn}(v)$ grows with $k(v)$, while a disassortative graph shows the opposite. For directed graphs the `source=` argument picks *whose* neighbors to enumerate (successors, predecessors, or both) and `target=` picks *which* degree to average over them, so the four combinations answer different questions about upstream and downstream mixing. Isolated nodes get a value of $0$ by convention. A weighted extension exists (Barrat et al., 2004) but is not yet implemented here. ## Examples {.doc-examples} **Path Graph - Undirected** In a 5-node path, each end node has one neighbor of degree `2`, giving an average neighbor degree of `2.0`; the second node has two neighbors of degree `1` and `2`, averaging to `1.5`: ::: {#0f8193f0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(5): g.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(4): g.add_edge(str(i), str(i+1)) g.average_neighbor_degree(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {5: 2.0, 3: 2.0, 1: 2.0, 4: 1.5, 2: 1.5} ``` ::: ::: **Directed Graph - Different source/target combinations** `source=` picks which neighbors to look at, and `target=` picks how their degree is measured -- so "out-out" and "in-in" can tell very different stories about the same graph: ::: {#5808994e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_node(label='A') g.add_node(label='B') g.add_node(label='C') g.add_edge('A', 'B') g.add_edge('B', 'C') g.add_edge('C', 'A') g.average_neighbor_degree(source="out", target="out", return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {1: 1.0, 3: 1.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#40e20c12 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.average_neighbor_degree(source="in", target="in", return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 1.0, 3: 1.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: **Store in Graph and Chain** ::: {#73dac3ef .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label='A') .add_node(label='B') .add_node(label='C') .add_edge('A', 'B') .add_edge('B', 'C') .average_neighbor_degree(attr_name='knn') ) g.get_node_attrs('knn') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {2: 1.0, 3: 2.0, 1: 2.0} ``` ::: :::
